Name: Two filter criteria applied together return only matching data
Description: Step 7a: filter by Employment Status AND Job Title, then verify the DATA in every returned row honours both criteria.

Name: The updated values survive a page refresh
Description: Step 6a: reload the record and confirm the edit did not revert.

Name: The updated values survive navigating away and back
Description: Step 6b: leave the employee record entirely, return to it, and confirm the update is still there -- including in the employee list, which reads from a different query.

Name: Apply Leave renders correctly for the account entitlement state
Description: Documents the environment constraint that makes the self-service Apply screen unusable for the Admin account, and pins it so a change in entitlement is noticed.

Name: Creating an employee without a last name is rejected
Description: Example A: submit Add Employee with the required Last Name empty. Expect an inline 'Required' message, no navigation, and no employee created.

Name: The submitted leave request can be located afterwards
Description: Step 8b: find the submitted request in the Leave List and verify its employee, type, date range and day count -- proving it was persisted, not just announced.

Name: The created employee can be found again in the employee list
Description: Step 4a: prove persistence by finding the new employee through the employee list, not by trusting the creation toast.

Name: An employee is created and entitled so leave can be assigned to them
Description: Creates a dedicated employee and grants a leave entitlement, so the leave request does not depend on pre-existing shared data.

Name: Valid credentials sign in and land on the dashboard
Description: Step 1b: login succeeds, the dashboard renders, and the signed-in user is identified.

Name: The created employee record opens and shows the data it was created with
Description: Step 4b: open the record from the list and verify name, employee id and that the detail tabs are reachable.

Name: An over-length name is rejected by the employee form
Description: Example B: enter a first name beyond the field's 30-character limit and expect the form to reject it rather than silently truncating or storing it.

Name: A new employee is created from generated data
Description: Step 3: create an employee with runtime-generated data and verify the success notification and the generated employee id.

Name: A leave request is submitted for calculated dates
Description: Step 8a: submit a leave request using a runtime-calculated date range and verify the success notification.

Name: Clearing the filters restores the full result set
Description: Step 7b: Reset clears every criterion and the unfiltered total returns.

Name: A leave request whose end date precedes its start date is rejected
Description: Example C: submit Assign Leave with To Date before From Date and expect the form to refuse it.

Name: Searching by name returns only employees matching that name
Description: Step 2: an employee that already exists is located by name and every returned row is verified against the search criteria.

Name: Invalid credentials are rejected with a clear message
Description: An additional negative scenario: a wrong password is refused, the user stays on the login page, and the message does not disclose which field was wrong.

Name: Login page renders with username, password and Login button
Description: Step 1a: the login page and each of its three required controls are present.

Name: Employee fields can be edited and the update is confirmed
Description: Step 5: change first name and employee id to new values, save, and verify both the success notification and the values on screen.
